output:
I'll start by reading the guide and the package layout.

The last call was cut off before it ran. I'll probe how the original code fails on out-of-range values.

That call was cut off too, so I'll make the module edits one at a time.

I'll redo that one edit, and from here on I'll run the edits sequentially.

Now roster.

Tests pass and no forbidden calls remain outside `timeparse.py`. Next I'll fuzz the new code against the original copy, which I saved in `/tmp/orig`.

I'll write the fuzz script to a file first, then run it.

Next is the same comparison through the CLI, on quirky site folders and several machine time zones.

Meanwhile, I'll write the tests for `timeparse`.

All date and time parsing now lives in `deskstats/timeparse.py`, with the exact public names from the guide. The other modules delegate to it and keep their public functions. `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.

The 31 tests pass with `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, including the new `tests/test_timeparse.py`. I compared the new code against a copy of the original package, using random and edge-case inputs (huge years, `nan`/`inf`, half-way milliseconds, `24:00`, Unicode digits) under three different machine time zones. There were no differences in results or error types.

I also ran 4200 CLI runs: every command, format and window option, including invalid ones, on 42 site folders, under four machine time zones. Standard output and exit status matched in every run. The only difference was in the traceback lines of inputs that already crashed the original. I then gave the helper exception classes the builtin names, so the last traceback line of the one case I re-checked is now identical. I did not re-run the full 4200-run comparison after that last change.

Behaviour I kept as it was, without fixing:
- **Roster years:** a negative two-digit year such as `-1` becomes 1999.
- **Crashes:** some bad inputs still crash the run with a traceback rather than a clean error. Examples are `1e999` in `calls.log`, `Infinity` or `1e30` in `chats.jsonl`, and a year or hour too large for a C int in `roster.txt`. Direct callers of `timeparse` see these as `ValueError` as well as the original error type. The loaders re-raise them, so the CLI still crashes as before.
- **Rounding:** calls truncate toward zero and chats round halves to even, in binary floating point.
- **Closures:** a closures date containing a hyphen is read as ISO, otherwise as the US form, so `2026-W11-1` and `20260310` are accepted.
- **Window end:** `--until` still ends at `23:59:59`, so a record at 23:59:59.5 on that day is left out.

One thing I could not make machine-independent is a `%Z` in a layout. Python's `strptime` itself checks `%Z` against the machine's zone names. The sheet layouts don't use `%Z`.

command_result.command: cd /app && git status 2>&1 | head -3; find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | grep -v pyc | head -100; cat docs/timeparse.md; wc -l deskstats/*.py docs/*.md

cd /app/deskstats && for f in __init__ __main__ errors site tickets escalations calls chats roster closures cli report; do echo "=== $f"; cat -A $f.py | sed 's/\$$//' ; done; cat ../docs/cli.md ../docs/sources.md ../docs/changelog.md
cd /app/deskstats && cat roster.py closures.py cli.py; sed -n 1,120p report.py

cd /app && sed -n 120,135p deskstats/report.py; cat tests/test_sources.py | head -80; grep -n "import\|timeparse" tests/test_cli.py | head -20; python --version; grep -rn "datetime\|date\b\|time\b\|timezone" deskstats/report.py | head -40

cd /app/deskstats && python - <<'EOF'
import re
p='roster.py'; s=open(p).read()
a=s.index('def parse_day'); b=s.index('def parse_line')
new='''def parse_day(text: str) -> date:
    """HR writes the day first. A two-digit year is in this century."""
    return timeparse.parse_day(text, timeparse.DMY)


def parse_clock(day: date, text: str, tz: tzinfo) -> datetime:
    """HH:MM on that day at the site; 24:00 is the midnight that ends the day."""
    return timeparse.at_clock(day, text, tz)


'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
s=s.replace('from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta, tzinfo','from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, tzinfo')
s=s.replace('from deskstats.errors','from deskstats import timeparse\nfrom deskstats.errors')
s=s.replace('''        try:
            out.append(parse_line(line, tz))
        except ValueError:''','''        try:
            out.append(parse_line(line, tz))
        except (OverflowError, OSError):
            raise  # not a line that cannot be read: it ends the run as it always did
        except ValueError:''')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='closures.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''    if "-" in text:
        return date.fromisoformat(text)
    return datetime.strptime(text, "%m/%d/%Y").date()''','''    if "-" in text:
        return timeparse.parse_day(text, timeparse.YMD)
    return timeparse.parse_day(text, timeparse.MDY)''')
s=s.replace('from datetime import date, datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\n','from datetime import date\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom deskstats import timeparse\n')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='cli.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('return date.fromisoformat(text)','return timeparse.parse_day(text, timeparse.YMD)')
s=s.replace('''    start = datetime.combine(since, time(0), site.tz) if since is not None else None
    end = datetime.combine(until, time(23, 59, 59), site.tz) if until is not None else None''','''    start = timeparse.day_start(since, site.tz) if since is not None else None
    end = timeparse.day_start(until, site.tz) + timedelta(hours=23, minutes=59, seconds=59) if until is not None else None''')
s=s.replace('from datetime import date, datetime, time\n','from datetime import date, timedelta\n')
s=s.replace('from deskstats import report\n','from deskstats import report, timeparse\n')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='report.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('midnight = datetime.combine(day + timedelta(days=1), time(0), tz)','midnight = timeparse.day_start(day + timedelta(days=1), tz)')
s=s.replace('from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta','from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta')
s=s.replace('from deskstats import calls, chats, closures, escalations, roster, tickets','from deskstats import calls, chats, closures, escalations, roster, tickets, timeparse')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -rnE 'strptime|fromisoformat|fromtimestamp|combine|timestamp|datetime\(|date\(|time\(|timezone\(|replace\(|import time|calendar|email' *.py | grep -v '^timeparse'; cd .. && python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -4

cd /tmp && python - <<'EOF'

s=s[:a]+'''    except BaseException as e:
        if isinstance(e, OverflowError): k = 'Overflow'
        elif isinstance(e, OSError): k = 'OSError'
        elif isinstance(e, ValueError): k = 'Value'
        else: k = type(e).__name__
        return ('err', k)

'''+s[b:]
open('fuzz.py','w').write(s)
EOF
python fuzz.py 2>&1 | tail -40

cd /tmp && python - <<'EOF'
exec(open('fuzz.py').read().split('random.seed(1)')[0])
print(orig['site'].__file__, new['site'].__file__)
from collections import Counter
c=Counter()
for t in ['09/03/26','9/3/-1','1/1/99999999999999999999','1e999','nan','24:00']:
    print(t, call(orig['roster'].parse_day,t), call(new['roster'].parse_day,t), call(orig['calls'].parse_epoch,t), call(new['calls'].parse_epoch,t))
EOF
TZ=America/New_York python fuzz.py | tail -3; TZ=Asia/Kolkata python fuzz.py | tail -3

cd /app && python - <<'EOF'
p='tests/test_timeparse.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('"1/1/0"[:4]','"1/1/"')
a=s.index('class Machine'); b=s.index('if __name__')
new='''class Machine(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_machine_zone_does_not_matter(self):
        code = (
            "from datetime import date, timedelta, timezone\\n"
            "from deskstats import timeparse as tp\\n"
            "z = timezone(timedelta(hours=1))\\n"
            "print(tp.from_epoch('1772442902.75', tp.SECONDS, tp.TRUNCATE).isoformat())\\n"
            "print(tp.from_epoch(-1500, tp.MILLIS, tp.NEAREST_EVEN).isoformat())\\n"
            "print(tp.parse_instant('2026-03-08T02:30:00', z).isoformat())\\n"
            "print(tp.at_clock(date(2026, 3, 8), '24:00', z).isoformat())\\n"
            "print(tp.day_start(date(2026, 3, 8), z).isoformat())\\n"
        )
        root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
        outputs = set()
        for zone in ["UTC", "America/New_York", "Asia/Kolkata", "Pacific/Auckland"]:
            env = dict(os.environ, TZ=zone, PYTHONPATH=root)
            done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
            outputs.add(done.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(len(outputs), 1)


'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
s=s.replace('import os\nimport time\nimport unittest','import os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nimport unittest')
open(p,'w').write(s)
